item.title: The Santa Cruz life guard who performed this rescue of drowning boy in massive churning surf is 16 years old
item.description: Photographer Scott was capturing images of Cypress Beach in California when he spotted a person's head appearing and disappearing amid the violent waves, so he rushed to alert one of the lifeguards. It turned out to be a 10-year-old boy who was riding the waves on his surfboard. The lifeguard grabbed hold of him, and despite the strength and ferocity of the waves, he clung to him tightly. Some people tried to help but were knocked down by the waves, so they backed away in fear. However, the lifeguard persisted until he rescued the boy. The most thrilling part of the story is that the lifeguard was only in his first season on the job.

item.title: Your Phone Isn't a Suitcase. It's Your Entire Fucking Life.
item.description: Encryption isn't suspicious. It's what responsible people do when they understand that the most valuable thing they own isn't the phone—it's everything inside it. The truly dangerous idea isn't that someone can protect their own data. It's that governments increasingly expect access first and justification later. A warrant used to be a constitutional safeguard. Now we're apparently being told it's an optional courtesy. When your phone contains your medical records, banking, private conversations, location history, photos, work documents, passwords, and the digital blueprint of your life, pretending it's no different than a piece of luggage is complete bullshit. Privacy isn't about having something to hide. It's about recognizing that freedom disappears the moment the state assumes your entire life should be available on demand. Today it's someone else's encrypted phone. Tomorrow it's your cloud storage. Next week it's your messages. Eventually it's the expectation that refusing access is itself evidence. Authoritarianism rarely arrives wearing jackboots. It arrives carrying paperwork and insisting it's all perfectly routine. If using strong security becomes probable cause, then the right to privacy has already been quietly hollowed out. The lock isn't the crime. Demanding every door remain unlocked is. #Privacy #Encryption #GrapheneOS #DigitalRights #FourthAmendment #CivilLiberties #CyberSecurity #Surveillance #Freedom #Technology #Imgur
